plan.rationale: 'Trusts the most people' counts distinct trustees, so the measure is unweighted out-degree, with edges read as source trusts target. The weight meaning is unclear but does not affect a count. Out-strength is reported alongside to show whether trust intensity changes the ranking.

result.explanation: No single person stands out: the highest out-degree is 3, and the top 10 returned (T10, T100, T101, T102, T103, T104, T105, T106, T107, T108) all trust exactly 3 people. These ten are listed in node-ID order, which suggests the tie extends to more nodes than the top 10 shown, but the full count of tied nodes was not reported. I treated the graph as directed (an edge source → target means "source trusts target") and counted distinct trustees with unweighted out-degree over all 600 nodes, not just the largest component. When edge weights are summed (out-strength), the ranking changes: T564 leads with 30, followed by T180 and T341 with 29 each. So if "trusts the most" means trust intensity rather than number of people, the answer would be different. These rankings are exact; no approximation was used.
